decisions.reason: As a core new-generation printer shown on the home page and very close to the firm's established machinery offer, it carries high sunk development and reputational commitment, so management is likely to continue it.
Although narrower and software-based, it was publicly presented as an expansion of the software portfolio and fits the firm's digital inline printing direction, which encourages continued support.
This coder extends the existing marking portfolio to another surface type, so the firm can justify staying with it as a portfolio-completing product rather than admitting a failed launch.

The app is less central and likely less capital-intensive than the hardware lines, but as a named successor product that supports decoding and traceability, management still has reasons to persist for now.

An inline code verification system is closely aligned with the firm's stated move toward serialization and end-to-end traceability, making withdrawal relatively unlikely despite limited public visibility.
Because it was shown on the home page and strengthens the software layer around the installed printing base, management is likely to keep backing it rather than write off the launch.
